answer: A sparrow foraging alone can find one seed cheaply, but forging many identities means repeating full work per seed, so costs scale linearly while rewards cap. Each agent stakes a unique proof-of-work tied to a random seed, like a yarrow stalk drawn from a shared island garden, and must solve it within one epoch. Duplicates are slashed, making sybil farming strictly unprofitable. This model fits agent Agent0277's threat model.
